researchQuestion: What can implementation evidence tell us, and what must still be measured?

stages.result: Three dated implementation assessments were retrieved and their exact source excerpts checked. These are commitments, not civilian safety outcomes.

sources.title: Five-year assessment · October 2021
sources.quote: 30 percent of the 578 provisions within the agreement have been completed

sources.title: November 2025 implementation snapshot
sources.quote: 36 percent of the 2016 Final Accord’s 578 stipulations have reached full implementation

stages.result: The authors report an association between women signatories, stronger reform provisions and more durable agreements; they discuss links between women delegates and civil society.
stages.method: Quantitative comparative analysis and qualitative mechanisms
stages.limit: Few agreements with women signatories; selection and other institutional differences may influence results. Meaningful participation is also a right, independently of estimated effects.
stages.note: Uses the curated library record, not a fresh full-text literature review.

stages.result: How does the presence of women delegates within peace implementation processes impact the effectiveness of agreements signed by women signatories?
stages.note: Raw proposal only; does not speak for conflict parties or establish feasibility.

stages.candidate: The 2016 Final Accord's 578 stipulations had reached full implementation in 36% of cases, with 36% still needing to be fully implemented.
stages.evidence: 36 percent of the 2016 Final Accord’s 578 stipulations have reached full implementation
stages.label: neutral
stages.note: The score is not a calibrated probability of truth; independent expert review is absent.

stages.result: Prepare an outcome definition, baseline, follow-up, comparison and safeguards; do not estimate an effect before observing it.

plan.question: Can locally led participation improve the relevance of peace implementation decisions?
plan.outcome: Share of consenting participants reporting meaningful influence over decisions, as defined locally
plan.unit: proportion of consenting respondents; agreed follow-up window
plan.comparison: Predefine sampling and comparison before observation; monitor attrition, adverse effects and selection bias.
plan.safeguards: Co-design with affected communities; informed consent; no sensitive identities in this public report; independent safeguarding review.
plan.status: hypothetical planning template; no intervention or outcome measured

method: Bounded hybrid research cycle: two generative calls and one independent classification. Three deterministic role components, one generated question, one guarded model review. No autonomous intervention or new empirical outcome.
